name: APT15
affiliation_detail:
No DOJ indictment or formal government attribution to a specific Chinese intelligence agency has been published for APT15. The group is broadly attributed to China-based actors. Microsoft described NICKEL as a "China-based threat actor" and stated there is "often a correlation between Nickel's targets and China's geopolitical interests."  FireEye originally described Ke3chang operators as "Chinese-speaking APT actors." 
In July 2026, Intrusion Truth attributed APT15 to PLA 8th Technical Reconnaissance Base (Unit 61046),  based on their investigation into RedRelay anonymization network, which they observed being sold to Unit 61046.
description:
APT15 is a Chinese cyber espionage group that has been active since at least 2010, primarily targeting government, diplomatic, military, and NGO entities. 
The group is best known for "Operation Ke3chang" (2013), which documented systematic targeting of European foreign ministries during the Syria crisis. In 2021 a U.S. court ordered Microsoft to seize 42 domains used to target organizations in 29 countries. In 2023, Symatec reported that APT15 continued its focus on foreign ministried throughout 2022 and early 2023, leveraging a new backdoor called Backdoor.Graphican. 
The group's focus on diplomatic targets, foreign ministries, government intelligence, and human rights organizations across Latin America, Europe, and Asia is consistent with MSS intelligence collection priorities.  However, no specific MSS bureau or front company has been publicly identified.
NCC group characterizes APT15 by its preference for "living off the land" — using native Windows commands and tools for reconnaissance and lateral movement rather than deploying extensive custom malware. Moreover, APT15 is notable for its persistence — NCC Group documented the group regaining access to a compromised UK government contractor within two weeks of remediation via a stolen VPN certificate. 
In July 2026, Intrusion Truth linked APT15 to PLA's "Unit 61046 ... otherwise known as the 8th TRB," through the investigation of anonymization tool RedRelay and subsequent leaked documents from a notetaking tool, which mentioned IP address hosting infrastructure "believed to be used exclusively by APT15."
Side note:
It is worth noting that Unit 61046 was pre-2015 known as the 8th Operational Bureau of the General Staff Department (GSD) Third Department.  Technical Reconnaissance Bueraus (TRB) were distinct from Operational Bureaus and were assigned to respective Military Regions (pre-reform). According to Project2049, "Third Department likely provides TRBs with policy guidance and tasking for collection and analysis." Notes investigated by Intrusion Truth mention 8th TRB of Strategic Support Force (SSF) and do not provide any dating.  However, SSF existed between 2015 and 2024, when it was replaced by Cyber Space Force (CSF). SSF 8th TRB was not previously noticed in open sources,  which however does not mean it did not exist. Moreover, 8th TRB was not observed as a part of CSF post-2024 reform. Again, not meaning it does not exist, given the secrecy of PLA.

campaigns.name: Operation Ke3chang (European Foreign Ministries)
campaigns.description: FireEye documented systematic targeting of European ministries of foreign affairs (MFAs) by Chinese-speaking APT actors. The campaign leveraged spear phishing with themes related to the Syria crisis to deliver BS2005, BMW, and MyWeb backdoors. FireEye accessed one of 23 C2 servers and found evidence of targeting across multiple European countries. Activity was traced back to at least 2010, including targeting related to a G20 meeting concerning the Irish debt crisis. After the December 2013 report publication, attackers continued with updated MyWeb variants and new infrastructure, including domains referencing French media outlets (Le Monde, Telerama).

campaigns.name: Indian Embassy Targeting (TidePool)
campaigns.description: Palo Alto Unit 42 discovered ongoing Ke3chang campaigns targeting Indian embassy personnel worldwide using the TidePool malware, an evolution of BS2005. Spear phishing emails used decoy documents referencing an annual report filed by over 30 Indian embassies. Delivered via CVE-2015-2545 exploit in MHTML documents.

campaigns.name: UK Government Contractor Compromise (RoyalCli/RoyalDNS)
campaigns.description: NCC Group responded to an active compromise of a UK government contractor by APT15. Sensitive documents related to UK government departments and military technology were stolen. APT15 used BS2005 alongside new backdoors RoyalCli and RoyalDNS. After NCC Group's initial remediation, APT15 regained access within two weeks via the corporate VPN using a stolen VPN certificate extracted from a compromised host, deploying the DNS-based RoyalDNS backdoor. NCC Group recovered over 200 attacker commands showing extensive use of living-off-the-land techniques. Tools included Mimikatz (for Kerberos golden tickets), WinRAR, and the bespoke spwebmember SharePoint dumping tool.

campaigns.name: European Diplomatic Missions (Ketrican/Okrum)
campaigns.description: ESET tracked Ke3chang activity across Central and South America and Europe from 2015 through 2019, discovering the previously unknown Okrum backdoor (active since December 2016) and multiple generations of Ketrican malware (BS2005 evolution). Targets included diplomatic missions in Slovakia, Belgium, Chile, Guatemala, and Brazil. ESET established code lineage connecting Ketrican, Okrum, RoyalDNS, and BS2005.

sources.title: Okrum: Ke3chang group takes aim at diplomatic missions

campaigns.name: NICKEL Global Campaign (Microsoft Domain Seizure)
campaigns.description: Microsoft tracked NICKEL/APT15 operations targeting governments, diplomatic entities, and NGOs across 29 countries in Central/South America, the Caribbean, Europe, and North America. The group exploited unpatched Exchange Server, SharePoint, and VPN appliances for initial access. Microsoft obtained a court order from the Eastern District of Virginia to seize 42 domains. NICKEL deployed hard-to-detect malware (including Leeson backdoor) for surveillance and data theft, used Mimikatz and WDigest for credential harvesting, and conducted automated, scheduled data collection and exfiltration.

campaigns.name: SPACEHOP Activity (ORB Network Usage)
campaigns.description: MITRE ATT&CK documents a campaign where Ke3chang utilized an ORB (operational relay box) network — a mesh of compromised devices and VPS infrastructure — for reconnaissance and vulnerability exploitation. Mandiant/Google Cloud documented this as part of broader research into China-nexus espionage use of ORB networks.
